Stage 3 Cloud Deployment Summary

Azure Blob Storage, Functions & Static Web Apps

Author: Yuandong Yang · Stage 3  |  Verified: 2026-11-06
This page summarises the Stage 3 Azure deployment and its live evidence. Person numbering follows the team’s division of work.

01 / Delivery at a Glance

2live URLs (API + dashboard)
3core Azure services
16deployment screenshots
1resource group, one-command teardown

Stage 3 of division.md takes the Stage 1 backend and the Stage 2 dashboard to the cloud. The dataset moves from a local CSV to a private Azure Blob Storage container, the API runs on a consumption-plan Azure Function App, and the dashboard is served from Azure Static Web Apps — all inside one resource group, created and removed by deploy.sh and teardown.sh.

Status: Deployment verified on 2026-10-20. The live dashboard and the API both respond; the header shows a green “API Connected” pill and every data response carries metadata.execution_time_seconds. The storage connection string lives only in the Function App settings — never committed, never printed — and CORS is scoped at the host level to the dashboard origin only. The Static Web App is in eastus2 because Static Web Apps is not offered in canadacentral, where the rest of the resources live.

03 / Architecture

Browser→Azure Static Web Apps
(dashboard)→Azure Function App
/api→Azure Blob Storage
All_Diets.csv

Why this shape

  • Serverless compute. The workload is bursty and read-only, so a consumption-plan Function App costs nothing while idle and needs no VM or container.
  • Hosting separate from compute. Static assets are served by a CDN-backed host; only data requests reach the Function, so the dashboard stays fast and the Function scales on its own.
  • Private storage, no public blob URL. The browser never talks to Blob Storage. The Function is the only reader and authenticates with a connection string in app settings, so the container stays private.
  • Stateless Function, cached dataset. No database: the cleaned DataFrame is cached in worker memory and invalidated by the blob’s ETag.

Regions

Everything lives in one resource group, cpsy300-nutritional-insights-rg, in canadacentral — except the Static Web App, which is in eastus2 because Static Web Apps is not available in canadacentral. The split is an explicit, overridable variable in deploy.sh, not an inconsistency.

The browser reaches the API cross-origin over HTTPS; host-level CORS allows only the Static Web App origin, so no other site can call the Function.

04 / Azure Services Used

ServiceConfigurationRole
Resource Groupcpsy300-nutritional-insights-rg, canadacentralOne logical container for every resource, so the whole environment deploys, audits and deletes as a unit.
Storage AccountStorageV2, Standard_LRS, TLS 1.2 minimum, public blob access disabledDurable, cheap object store for the dataset; also backs the Function App’s own AzureWebJobsStorage.
Blob container datasetsPrivate; holds All_Diets.csvKeeps the dataset out of the repo and the deployment package; private means no anonymous URL exists.
Function Appcpsy300-nutrition-api, Python 3.11, Functions v4, Linux consumptionServerless HTTP API running the cleaning and aggregation code on demand; pay-per-execution and automatic scale-out.
Static Web Appcpsy300-nutrition-dashboard, Free SKU, eastus2, created unlinkedPublic HTTPS hosting for the dashboard with a default hostname; unlinked so no GitHub token is needed.
Function App settingsAZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING, BLOB_CONTAINER_NAME, BLOB_NAMEExternalises all configuration and the one secret; nothing environment-specific is hard-coded.
CORS configurationHost-level allowed origins, scoped to the SWA originLets the dashboard call the API from its own origin without opening the API to every website.
Application InsightsProvisioned with the Function AppCaptures logs and exceptions — where internal error detail goes instead of into HTTP responses.

05 / Deployment Pipeline

One command, ./deploy.sh, runs seven idempotent steps. Re-running it updates the existing resources and reuses the storage account already in the group instead of creating a second one.

[1/7] Resource group     cpsy300-nutritional-insights-rg   (canadacentral)
[2/7] Storage + dataset  cpsy300nutrition  ->  container "datasets" (private)  ->  upload All_Diets.csv
[3/7] Function App       cpsy300-nutrition-api  (Python 3.11, Functions v4, consumption)
                         app settings: connection string, container name, blob name
[4/7] Publish backend    func azure functionapp publish   ->  smoke-tested
[5/7] Static Web App     cpsy300-nutrition-dashboard  (Free, eastus2, unlinked)
[6/7] Build + deploy FE  inject the live API URL into a throwaway build/, then swa deploy
[7/7] Scope CORS         remove '*', allow only the dashboard origin, then smoke-test

Function App : https://cpsy300-nutrition-api.azurewebsites.net/api
Dashboard    : https://salmon-ocean-0ce94150f.4.azurestaticapps.net/

The storage connection string is written straight into the Function App settings and never printed, so it cannot leak into terminal scrollback, a screenshot or a screen recording; deploy.sh prints the az command to retrieve it on demand instead. Every name, region and runtime version is an overridable environment variable.

07 / Challenges and Solutions

ChallengeSolution
Duplicate CORS headers
Host-level CORS and handler-written CORS produced the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header twice, which browsers reject.		Give exactly one layer ownership: the host allows only the SWA origin and the function code emits no CORS headers at all.
A 1.21 MB response on every load
/api/recipes returned all 7,806 rows on every load and filter change — slow and costly on a consumption plan.		Page server-side (default 50, hard cap 500); return total / total_pages; a fresh request per page click. Typical response is now tens of KB.
Re-downloading and re-cleaning the CSV each request
Doing it per request dominated response time, but caching blindly would ignore a re-uploaded CSV.		Cache the cleaned DataFrame keyed by the blob ETag; one cheap metadata call per request; dataset_from_cache exposes the path taken.
The API URL is unknown until deploy time
The Function URL only exists after the Function App is created, and hard-coding it breaks other environments.		index.html ships a __FUNCTION_API_URL__ placeholder; deploy.sh substitutes it into a throwaway build/, verifies it, and deploys only that. Sources stay clean.
A silent fallback that looked live
An earlier build rendered non-live data behind a subtle badge — actively misleading.		Fallback is now the real Project 1 output behind a prominent banner; any failure switches the whole view, so live and fallback data never mix.
Static Web Apps region availability
az staticwebapp create fails in canadacentral, where everything else lives.		A separate SWA_LOCATION=eastus2 for the Static Web App while LOCATION=canadacentral governs the rest; both overridable and documented.
A Static Web App without a GitHub token
Linking a SWA to GitHub needs an over-privileged personal access token.		Create the SWA unlinked and deploy with the swa CLI using a deployment token from az staticwebapp secrets list — no GitHub credential.
Keeping the docs and code in sync
An earlier draft and the deployed code had drifted apart on endpoint counts, correlation signs and resource names.		Reconciled both against a verified audit: corrected the counts and signs, aligned every resource name with deploy.sh, and added the /api/clusters route to the cloud backend so the live API matches the Stage 1 contract and the dashboard’s clusters chart.

08 / Teardown and Cost

cd stage3
./teardown.sh                              # deletes cpsy300-nutritional-insights-rg and everything in it
az group list --query "[].name" -o tsv     # confirm the group is gone
Run teardown as soon as the evidence is captured. Azure bills by the hour and by the request, so a resource group left running over a weekend costs more than the whole demo did. The delete is irreversible: the uploaded dataset, the Function App settings and the Static Web App all go with it. Re-running deploy.sh rebuilds everything, but the Static Web App gets a new hostname, so any URL already written into a report or a slide stops working.
